subject.title: [Bug]: cron agentTurn returns before foreground Bash subprocess completes — long-running executors are killed mid-stream, leaving partial state and a placeholder digest

question: Should isolated cron `agentTurn` on `claude-cli` block terminal success on foreground native tool completion, fail/telemetry-mark runs with pending native work, or route this pattern to command cron instead?
rationale: The fix crosses cron success semantics, Claude CLI process cleanup safety, and operator-facing delivery truth, and a cleanup opt-out or new telemetry surface would be a product/runtime contract change.

options.title: Block or fail pending native tool work
options.body: Make cron `agentTurn` treat pending foreground native tool work as non-terminal, either waiting within the job timeout or recording a typed error/pending state before cleanup.

options.title: Telemetry first
options.body: Keep cleanup behavior but add explicit run-record diagnostics for killed or pending CLI-owned native tool work so monitors no longer see a green run.

options.title: Route scripts to command cron
options.body: Document and enforce that long deterministic shell scripts should use command cron, leaving model-backed `agentTurn` for digesting already-materialized state.

recommendation.title: Block or fail pending native tool work
recommendation.body: Make cron `agentTurn` treat pending foreground native tool work as non-terminal, either waiting within the job timeout or recording a typed error/pending state before cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has broad history across cron execution and process-supervisor surfaces and is the best available owner for the lifecycle/product tradeoff.
